mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team B produces high shot volume (all-prior and recent) while Team A's shots-on-target FOR has risen in recent matches relative to all-prior, and Team B's shots-on-target AGAINST has fallen in recent matches relative to all-prior. Measure how this joint configuration relates to corner and goal outcomes.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team's shot volume is high but the opposing team's on-target efficiency is rising, corner kicks generated by the high-volume team are suppressed relative to what shot volume alone would predict, because more attacks are resolved on target rather than deflected wide.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's shot volume is structurally high relative to its shots-on-target conversion, while Team A's recent shots-on-target rate has risen sharply relative to its all-prior baseline. The joint relationship between one side's shot volume and the other side's on-target efficiency — measured as a cross-team ratio — may predict corner and goal outcomes differently than either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) across two different teams simultaneously — not reducible to a single observable with one band. The asymmetry (Team B's volume vs. Team A's on-target efficiency) is a cross-team, cross-observable relationship.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team B's home corner production rate versus its away rate, and Team A's corner-concession rate versus the competition baseline, while also accounting for Team A's possession deficit (away possession lower than home). Since Team A is home here, Team B is the away side — so Team B's away corner rate applies. Measure whether the combination of Team A's above-average corner concession and Team B's below-home-level away corner production yields a corner total that saturates or is suppressed relative to the sum of individual baselines.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: The joint configuration of a high-conceding home team facing a visitor whose away corner production is substantially lower than their home rate produces a corner total that is lower than Team A's concession rate alone would suggest, indicating a saturation or suppression effect from the venue-driven production gap.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B generates substantially more corners at home than away, while Team A concedes more corners overall than the competition average. The joint interaction of Team B's venue-conditioned corner production and Team A's corner-concession rate — measured together — may produce a non-additive corner total that differs from what each observable predicts independently.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves two distinct observables (corner_kicks and possession) and two distinct opponent-descriptor dimensions simultaneously (venue-split production for Team B and concession rate for Team A), which is not reducible to a single observable with one coarse band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where both Team A and Team B have second-half goal rates exceeding their first-half rates. Measure whether matches where both teams exhibit this second-half scoring skew produce a first-half goal total that is suppressed relative to the full-match average, and a second-half total that is elevated — beyond what either team's individual half-split alone would predict.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When both teams independently show a second-half scoring skew, the first half of their head-to-head encounter is more likely to be low-scoring and the second half elevated, with the joint effect being stronger than either team's individual skew would imply additively.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's goals are skewed toward the second half (more second-half goals than first-half goals), while Team B also scores more in the second half than the first. The joint within-match scoring distribution of both teams — measured as the ratio of second-half to first-half goals for each side — may interact to produce a distinctive half-level goal pattern that differs from what full-match goal rates predict.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a within-match state (half-level) dependence requiring half-resolution data, and it involves a joint relationship across both teams' half-split goal distributions simultaneously — not a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition jointly on Team B's above-average yellow card rate (both FOR and AGAINST) and Team A's near-average foul rate. Measure whether this asymmetric configuration — where one team is a high-card accumulator and the other is not — produces a second-half card total (cards_2h) that is elevated beyond what the competition baseline or either team's individual card rate predicts, particularly given that second-half card rates are already above the per-half average in this competition.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When one team is a structurally high card accumulator and the opposing team is not, second-half card totals rise with the high-card team's yellow card rate in a way that is not symmetric — the joint asymmetry amplifies second-half card accumulation beyond what a simple average of both teams' rates would predict.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B accumulates substantially more yellow cards than Team A and more than the competition average, while Team A's foul rate is near or below the competition average. The joint relationship between one team's foul production and the other team's card accumulation — measured as an asymmetric cross-team pairing — may predict second-half card totals differently than either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a genuine joint relationship across two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) and an asymmetric cross-team pairing, combined with a within-match state (second half). It is not reducible to one observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Condition on the joint state where Team A's recent possession is substantially below its home baseline and all-prior average, while Team A's recent offsides FOR has risen sharply above its all-prior average. Measure whether this joint configuration (low possession + high offsides) is associated with a suppression of Team A's corner and shot production relative to what its all-prior rates would predict, and whether Team B's corner and shot production rises correspondingly.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When a team's possession drops sharply while its offside rate rises, its corner and shot production is suppressed relative to its baseline, and the opposing team's corner and shot production rises — the joint possession-offside divergence is a stronger predictor of this asymmetric production shift than either observable alone.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's possession has declined sharply in recent matches relative to its all-prior baseline (and especially relative to its home baseline), while Team B's possession is relatively stable. Simultaneously, Team A's offsides FOR has risen sharply in recent matches. The joint relationship between a team's possession deficit and its rising offside rate — two distinct observables moving in opposite directions — may indicate a structural shift toward a counter-attacking regime that affects shots, corners, and goals in a non-linear way.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This involves a genuine joint relationship between two distinct observables (possession and offsides) for the same team, where both are moving simultaneously in ways that suggest a regime shift. It also involves an asymmetric cross-team production consequence. This is not reducible to a single observable with one band or a simple recent-vs-long-run comparison of one metric.
